newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West electric reliability compact proposed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West electric reliability compact proposed.

text.p: The Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) has endorsed a compact of mandatory compliance with electric system reliability standards, the WSCC said Wednesday.
The WSCC - one of 10 electric reliability councils in the U.S. - is a voluntary organization of 96 utilities and power marketers which aims to enhance reliability of the western power grid.
The WSCC said it hopes to replace this volunatary system with a new framework that will clarify and strengthen its role and authority.

Jan Packwood, WSCC chairman and executive vice president of Idaho Power Co., said in a statement there is a growing economic incentive as the electric industry restructures and competition increases for industry participants to minimize the costs and other requirements associated with meeting reliability needs.

After two major power outages hit western states in July and August, a wide range of industry participants, including most large utilities, have called for a system of mandatory reliability compliance.
A WSCC task force is expected to propose specific steps to implement the plan.
